day_shape: Trump alleges Iranian ceasefire violation after Strait of Hormuz drone attacks on ships, Zurich talks establish a US-Iran Hormuz communications line, IDF kills seven Hezbollah operatives in southern Lebanon, and UK MPs table Bahá'í questions.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz incident and Zurich track
threads.summary: Trump accused Iran of a 'foolish violation of the ceasefire agreement' following drone attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, per Jerusalem Post. IRIB said the Zurich final statement established a US-Iran communications line for the Strait and a 60-day waiver of passage fees, with Bloomberg reporting Oman told Europeans ships must pay service fees.

threads.label: US-Iran MoU and IAEA access
threads.summary: Iran International and Jerusalem Post coverage examined the US-Iran memorandum of understanding, with the IAEA chief saying the accord grants inspectors access despite Iranian hopes to keep some sites off-limits. IRIB reported Araghchi briefed his UK counterpart on the latest negotiations, while Tehran rejected a joint US-GCC statement as interventionist.

threads.label: Southern Lebanon strikes and clashes
threads.summary: The IDF said its air force killed seven Hezbollah operatives moving weapons near Manzala in southern Lebanon, and reported four soldiers including two officers wounded in a separate clash overnight. Israeli ministers complained in cabinet that soldiers are unduly restricted by the ceasefire, while flyers were dropped over Mansouri near Tyre.

threads.label: Ashura mourning and protest counter-memory
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press carried heavy Ashura coverage including millions reported in Karbala's Tuwairej ceremony and a message from Mojtaba Khamenei pledging to stand under the Imam's banner. Iran International reported Iranians repurposing Muharram mourning to commemorate victims of January's protests, and traced deaths to Gharazi Hospital in Isfahan.

threads.label: IRGC-linked hacking arrest and UK questions
threads.summary: Montenegrin police and the FBI arrested an Iranian-Turkish national wanted in the US over a hacking campaign targeting more than 150 universities allegedly benefiting the IRGC, per Iran International and Jerusalem Post. Liberal Democrat MP Tom Morrison tabled two FCDO questions on persecution of the Bahá'í community in Iran.

events.title_en: Millions of mourners in Karbala; observance of traditional Tuwairej ceremony on Ashura Coinciding with Husayni Ashura, Karbala witnessed the presence of millions of pilgrims and mourning delegations. The traditional Tuwairej ceremony was held with the participation of tens of thousands of people. Religious delegations and participants in these ceremonies staged traditional mourning ceremonies for the Master and Commander of Martyrs, including the Tuwairej ceremony, which is one of the oldest and most authentic ceremonial mourning practices in Iraq and especially in the city of Karbala, held with the participation of tens of thousands of people. Participants in this ceremony, after holding noon and afternoon prayers in a reenactment of events related to women and children taken captive in the Karbala incident, walked several kilometres

events.title_en: Velayati: The stability of Arabs on the shores of the Persian Gulf is indebted to Iran's management of the Strait of Hormuz The international adviser to the leader of the revolution, referring to the biased statement of the Cooperation Council of the Persian Gulf in cyberspace, wrote: The stability today of Arabs on the shores of the Persian Gulf is indebted to Iran's century-long management of the Strait of Hormuz. The West has produced nothing but savagery and plunder for the region. Bordering residents and political children of the region are not satisfied with ordered statements and should know: Your survival is from the crumbs of this table. In the rearrangement of grand equations, small bordering states have no place at the table; they are eliminated and their strategic existence depends on Tehran's tolerance threshold.

events.title_en: Complete removal of worn-out buses from the capital's fleet by the end of 1406 CEO of Tehran and suburbs unified bus company: The programme for the complete removal of worn-out buses from the fleet by the end of 1406 has been targeted. Of the 3,244 buses active in the Tehran bus company fleet, 942 are considered worn-out. According to planning, the capital needs approximately 7,000 buses. The average age of the active buses in Tehran's bus company is currently 11.3 years, and with the implementation of modernisation programmes, this figure will gradually decline.

events.title_en: The air force attacked earlier today and killed seven elements of the Hezbollah terrorist organisation who were transporting combat equipment near the security area where IDF forces operate in southern Lebanon. The terrorists transported combat equipment into a building in the Manara area that was used as a combat and observation point.
events.summary_en:
The air force attacked earlier today and killed seven elements of the Hezbollah terrorist organisation who were transporting combat equipment near the security area where IDF forces operate in southern Lebanon.

The terrorists transported combat equipment into a building in the Manara area that was used as a combat and observation point monitoring IDF forces. From inside the building, the saboteurs used the site for military purposes and prepared to target our forces

The activity of the saboteurs inside the site, along with the presence of combat equipment in it, posed a threat to our forces

The IDF will not allow the Hezbollah terrorist organisation to harm the citizens of the State of Israel or its forces, and will continue to work to eliminate any threats

events.title: The Israeli Air Force struck and killed seven Hezbollah operatives in southern Lebanon this morning, after they were identified transporting weapons near Israel's security zone, the military says. The IDF says the operatives were spotted by troops of the Egoz Commando Unit near the village of Manzala moving weapons into a structure "used as a combat and observation post" and to prepare to carry out attacks on troops. "The terrorists’ actions at the post alongside the presence of the weapons within it constituted a threat to the soldiers," the military says.

The Israeli Air Force struck and killed seven Hezbollah operatives in southern Lebanon this morning, after they were identified transporting weapons near Israel's security zone, the military says.

The IDF says the operatives were spotted by troops of the Egoz Commando Unit near the village of Manzala moving weapons into a structure "used as a combat and observation post" and to prepare to carry out attacks on troops.

"The terrorists’ actions at the post alongside the presence of the weapons within it constituted a threat to the soldiers," the military says.

A combat officer was moderately hurt in the incident, and another officer and the two soldiers were lightly hurt, the IDF says. They were taken to the hospital for treatment, and their families were notified. According to an IDF probe of the incident, at around 10 p.m. last night in the Beit Yahoun area, a Hezbollah operative who was hiding in a building threw a grenade at Israeli troops, causing the injuries. Within a few minutes, the forces returned fire, killing the operative, the probe finds. The IDF also struck several Hezbollah sites in the area
